digest.headline: Barclays raised its S&P 500 target to 7,950 as oil prices surged and Saudi oil production dropped to 1990 levels.

lede.b: Barclays lifted its target for the S&P 500 index, which tracks five hundred large companies, to 7,950 following strong second-quarter earnings. At the same time, high consumer price inflation and record diesel prices pressured the Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States that sets official interest rates, to weigh a rate hike. Saudi Arabia reduced its oil output to 6.24 million barrels a day, its lowest level since 1990, after Houthi drone strikes hit facilities. These energy shocks pushed Brent crude above $109 per barrel and caused India's Sensex index to plunge 1,734 points.
lede.i: Barclays raised its S&P 500 index target to 7,950 on the back of stronger second-quarter corporate profits. Concurrently, elevated inflation and record diesel prices increased pressure on the Federal Reserve to consider raising interest rates. In global energy markets, Saudi oil production dropped to 6.24 million barrels a day following drone and missile strikes, driving Brent crude above $109 per barrel. This surge in energy costs triggered a 1,734-point drop in India's Sensex index and a 1.1% decline in the rupee against the US dollar.
lede.a: Barclays revised its S&P 500 index target to 7,950, citing robust second-quarter earnings growth and an upgraded 2026 forecast. Concurrently, persistent inflation and record diesel prices amplified policy pressure on the Federal Reserve to contemplate rate hikes. Supply contractions pushed Saudi crude output to 6.24 million barrels a day, a level last seen in 1990, following strikes on Aramco infrastructure and Red Sea shipping disruptions. Brent crude surpassed $109 per barrel in response, precipitating a 1,734-point sell-off in the Indian Sensex and a 1.1% depreciation of the rupee.

stories.t: Sensex Plunges as Oil Prices Climb
stories.b: The Sensex is an index, which is a basket of major shares tracked to see how the stock market is doing. It plunged by 1,734 points to 74,781. The Nifty fell by 2.09% in its fifth straight weekly loss. Brent crude topped $109 per barrel, causing the rupee to slump 1.1% to 95.57.
stories.i: The Sensex plummeted 1,734 points to 74,781 while the Nifty dropped 2.09% for a fifth consecutive weekly decline. Brent crude surpassed $109 per barrel, erasing early-September gains. The rupee slumped 1.1% to 95.57 against the dollar amid surging energy costs.
stories.a: Equities suffered deep losses as the Sensex fell 1,734 points to 74,781 and the Nifty shed 2.09% to notch its fifth consecutive weekly decline. Brent crude breaking above $109 per barrel drove severe currency depreciation, pushing the rupee down 1.1% to 95.57. The macro shock of dearer imported energy transmitted directly into broader equity liquidations.
